newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania opposition forum launched after crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Albania opposition forum launched after crackdown.

text.p: Albania's opposition parties on Thursday launched a Forum for Democracy against the ruling right-wing Democrats as the government tightened its grip around the Balkan nation following a wave of protests.
The anti-government bloc, including the large Socialist Party, set up the forum following a police roundup of opposition activists across the country on charges of inciting recent unrest.
Sporadic protests over the past three weeks have been sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes, causing thousands of impoverished Albanians to lose almost everything they owned.
Seven opposition parties said in a joint statement they had formed an alliance to press for the resignation of the government in the wake of the huge investment scandal.

The Interior Ministry denied newspaper reports that police had detained hundreds of opposition figures, mainly in towns in the south where demonstrators last weekend set ablaze scores of government buildings and Democratic Party offices.
"The Interior Ministry denies...the newspaper reports speaking of 700 citizens detained by police," the ministry said in a statement.

It said 247 people had been brought in for questioning to help police with investigations into the troubles in Tirana, the southern towns of Berat, Fieri, Vlora and Korca, the central town of Lushnje and Diber in the east.
A ministry spokesman on Wednesday said there was no political motivation behind the detentions.
The Socialists accused the Democrats of intimidation and said they had imposed an effective state of emergency throughout the former communist state.
"Presently a de facto state of emergency has been established. Mass arrests have taken place," the secretary general of the Socialist Party, Rexhep Mejdani, told reporters.
Police for a second consecutive day broke up an anti-government demonstration in a soccer field on the outskirts of Tirana centre called by small rightist parties.
Police officers prevented around 200 people gathering in the field and pushed reporters, photographers and cameramen out of the field by force. Two people were believed arrested.

Azem Hajdari, a leader of the 1990 anti-communist revolt and now a senior trade union leader, on Wednesday pledged to carry on peaceful protests until the government had come up with a comprehensive solution to the investment fund crisis, which is believed to affect almost every Albanian.

President Sali Berisha, who co-founded the Democratic Party in 1990 with Hajdari and others, vowed that some pyramid scheme money locked in frozen funds in state banks will be gradually paid back to investors from next Wednesday.
But he said he could not guarantee that everyone would get every lek back, which may anger some investors facing ruin.

He suggested that some people may be given bank certificates or the chance of investment in enterprise zones. But with the credibility of Albania's finances already shaken, most people will continue to demand the return of hard cash.
